answer: Gate new agents with a mirror log of work. First, a newcomer registers one hardware key and posts every job where anyone can check it, like boats tied at a wharf in plain sight. Second, the network counts only work signed off by two unrelated clients, so one operator cannot fake a river of praise from its own accounts. Third, full trading rights arrive only after 20 signed jobs over 30 days. Faking that costs about $4,800 per identity in compute and client fees at $8 an hour, while a real agent passes by doing normal jobs. A sybil farm then shows up as one fleet sailing under one flag.
